_note: Pre-authored safety flow. Every step quotes or closely follows Ready.gov: Floods. The model may choose a branch but never writes or changes steps. Checked Nov 2, 2026.
title: Flood safety
question: What's your situation right now?
disclaimer: General guidance from Ready.gov and FloodSmart, not local emergency instructions. Always follow orders from local officials.

sources.name: FloodSmart: How do I start my flood claim?

branches.label: Water is rising near me
branches.hint: A flood warning, or water coming up

steps.title: Evacuate if told to
steps.text: Evacuate immediately, if told to do so. Never drive around barricades.

steps.title: Get higher
steps.text: Depending on the type of flooding, move to higher ground or a higher floor, or stay where you are.

steps.title: Stay out of the water
steps.text: Do not walk, swim or drive through flood waters. Turn Around, Don’t Drown.

steps.title: Keep listening
steps.text: Listen to EAS, NOAA Weather Radio or local alerting systems for current emergency information.

steps.title: Turn around
steps.text: Do not drive through flood waters. Just six inches of moving water can knock you down, and one foot of moving water can sweep your vehicle away.

steps.title: Avoid bridges over fast water
steps.text: Stay off bridges over fast-moving water. Fast-moving water can wash bridges away without warning.

steps.title: If water surrounds your car
steps.text: Stay inside your car if it is trapped in rapidly moving water. Get on the roof if water is rising inside the car.

steps.title: Call 911 now
steps.text: If you are experiencing a medical emergency, call 9-1-1.

steps.title: Go to the highest level
steps.text: Get to the highest level if trapped in a building. Do not climb into a closed attic to avoid getting trapped by rising floodwater.

steps.title: Signal for help
steps.text: Only get on the roof if necessary and once there, signal for help.

steps.title: Wait for the all-clear
steps.text: Return home only when authorities say it is safe.

steps.title: Watch for electricity
steps.text: Do not touch electrical equipment if it is wet or if you are standing in water. Turn off the electricity to prevent electric shock if it is safe to do so.

steps.title: Protect yourself
steps.text: Wear heavy work gloves, protective clothing and boots during cleanup. Avoid wading in floodwater, which can be contaminated and contain dangerous debris.

steps.title: Mold and health
steps.text: People with asthma and other lung conditions and/or immune suppression should not enter buildings with indoor water leaks or mold growth that can be seen or smelled. Children should not take part in disaster cleanup work.

steps.title: Document the damage
steps.text: Take photos and videos of your flood-damaged belongings and property for your insurance claim.
